## INCIDENT REPORT: MTA-2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 Address | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC Address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows Hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| Domain | lafontainebleu.org |
| Logged-in User | plucero |

### Malware Attribution

**Family:** Adwind RAT (Remote Access Trojan)

**Attribution Basis:** Behavioral signature match
- C2 beaconing pattern to bare-IP HTTP endpoint with `/foots.php` URI pattern (known Adwind C2 endpoint identifier)
- Multi-stage delivery chain: PowerShell > ZIP > JavaScript > DLL payload
- DLL file type and repeated GET/POST beaconing to single external C2 every 5-7 seconds
- Fake FedEx domain lure in delivery stage

### Indicators of Compromise

#### Command & Control Endpoints

| Type | Value | Port | Protocol | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IPv4 (C2 Server) | 72.5.43.29 | 80 | HTTP | Confirmed |

**C2 Behavior:** 1,844 packets sent to this endpoint; repetitive GET/POST requests to `/` and `/foots.php` beginning at packet timestamp 1723680719 (08:51:59 UTC); responses initially 200 OK then 400 Bad Request (no new commands issued).

#### Malicious Domains

| Domain | Resolution IP(s) | Purpose | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| quote.checkfedexexp.com | 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 | Payload delivery (ZIP download) | Confirmed |
| business.checkfedexexp.com | 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70 | Typosquatting FedEx (command domain) | Confirmed |

**Note:** Both domains typosquat legitimate FedEx infrastructure; used together in delivery chain.

#### Malicious URLs

| URL | Delivered Payload | File Hash (SHA256) |
|---|---|---|
| `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` | ZIP archive containing JavaScript | 798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5 |
| `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | PE32+ DLL (x86-64, GUI Windows) | b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6 |

#### Transferred Files & Hashes

| Filename | File Type | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| pas.ps1 | PowerShell script (obfuscated Base64) | 1513 bytes | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js | JavaScript (embedded in ZIP) | 6,990,020 bytes | dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c |
| 0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 | PE32+ DLL (GUI, x86-64) | 159,232 bytes | b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6 |
| osk | Binary data (likely registry hive or system artifact) | ? bytes | 1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f |

### Delivery Chain & Timeline

1. **Stage 1 (Delivery):** `pas.ps1` PowerShell script downloaded (obfuscated, uses base64 string encoding with octal/hex substitution). Delivers Base64-encoded command for stage 2.

2. **Stage 2 (Dropper):** PowerShell executes, downloads ZIP from `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70) at timestamp 1723680658.536866. ZIP contains `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` disguised as invoice PDF.

3. **Stage 3 (Payload):** JavaScript extracts and executes DLL payload from `72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` at timestamp 1723680719.744428.

4. **Stage 4 (C2 Beaconing):** DLL establishes persistent C2 connection to `72.5.43.29:80`, initiating beaconing to `/foots.php` and `/` endpoints at irregular 5-7 second intervals. Server responds with 200 OK initially, then 400 Bad Request (no active commands). Beaconing observed for entire capture duration (~1827 seconds).

### Summary

Victim workstation compromised by multi-stage Adwind RAT delivered via FedEx-impersonating domain. Malware maintains persistent C2 presence to bare-IP server; no command activity observed during capture window, but beacon interval and response pattern consistent with active C2 infrastructure awaiting operator input.
